faq.q: Do I actually need an RO water purifier in India?
faq.a: It depends on your input water. If your municipal supply or borewell has TDS above 500 ppm (most of India does), RO is the practical choice. Below 300 ppm, a UV-only purifier works and keeps minerals in the water. RO strips out everything — including the minerals that make water taste good — which is why TDS controllers and copper / mineral cartridges exist.

faq.q: What is the recovery rate and why does it matter?
faq.a: Recovery rate is the percentage of input water that becomes purified water. A 75% recovery RO turns 4 L of input into 3 L of purified water and wastes 1 L. A 50% recovery RO turns 4 L into 2 L and wastes 2 L. In water-scarce cities — Chennai, Bengaluru, parts of Mumbai — the higher recovery rate is worth a small premium. In areas with cheap piped water, the recovery rate is mostly a billing question.

faq.q: How often do I need to change the filters?
faq.a: For a typical Indian household (20–30 L/day), the sediment and carbon pre-filters need changing every 6 months, the RO membrane every 12–18 months, and the UV lamp every 12 months. The TDS controller and post-carbon filter usually run 12–18 months. Most brands offer annual maintenance contracts (AMC) at ₹1,500–₹3,000 that cover all of this plus a free service visit.

faq.q: Is the storage tank of 7–9 L really enough?
faq.a: For a family of 4–5, 8 L is the practical minimum. RO purifiers produce water slowly — usually 8–15 L per hour — so the tank is what you drink from during the day. Purely tankless RO units exist (they connect directly to a tap) but they have a much lower flow rate and aren't practical for Indian cooking volumes. If you have a large family or cook a lot of dal and rice, go for 9 L or larger.

faq.q: Can I install an RO purifier myself?
faq.a: Technically yes, but most brands require authorised installation for the warranty to hold. The install takes 30–60 minutes and typically involves a water-supply tap connector, a drain line, and a wall mount. The first service visit is usually free with a new purchase; the AMC kicks in from year 2.

body:
What actually matters in an RO water purifier in 2026

Choosing an RO water purifier in India used to be a brand question — Kent vs Pureit vs Aquaguard — and not much else. In 2026, the brands still matter (service network is the single biggest variable in real-world satisfaction), but the specifications have moved enough that the wrong pick can burn 25–30% of your water and leave you with tasteless output.

The three things that actually move the needle on an Indian household RO in 2026 are recovery rate, post-treatment, and service network reach. Litre capacity and tank size matter too, but the bigger 12 L tanks from sub-brands usually come with weaker membranes and lower recovery rates — you get more water but waste more of it.

If you only buy one thing from this list: the Kent Grand Plus (11016). Its 75% recovery rate is the best in this price band, the 9 L tank suits a family of 4–5, the UV+UF post-treatment handles municipal supply well, and Kent's service network is the widest in India with a 90-minute city SLA in most metros.

Recovery rate: the underrated water-saving spec

Recovery rate is the percentage of input water that becomes purified water. A 75% recovery RO turns 4 L of input into 3 L of purified water and wastes 1 L. A 50% recovery RO turns 4 L into 2 L and wastes 2 L. In water-scarce cities — Chennai, Bengaluru, parts of Mumbai — the higher recovery rate is worth a small premium. The Kent Grand Plus, LG Puricare, and a few newer Pureit models sit at 75%; most Aquaguard models and the older Eureka Forbes units sit at 55–60%. The difference compounds over a year: a 75% recovery RO in a 4-person household wastes ~120 L less per year than a 55% recovery unit.

Post-RO treatment: UV, UF, copper, mineral cartridges

RO strips out everything — bacteria, viruses, heavy metals, and the minerals that make water taste good. Post-RO treatment rebuilds some of that. UV disinfects the purified water and matters most for municipal supply where there's a real (if small) chance of post-RO contamination in the tank. UF is a secondary physical filter that catches any carbon or membrane fines. Copper cartridges (Pureit Copper+ Mineral) infuse copper ions into the water, which is a real thing in ayurvedic practice but used for taste and marketing more than verified health benefit. Mineral cartridges add calcium and magnesium back to bring the TDS up to a more drinkable 50–100 ppm range.

Service network beats specifications on paper

An RO purifier is one of the few home appliances that needs a service visit every 6–12 months to swap filters and sanitise the tank. A brand with great specs and a weak service network — almost every sub-₹8,000 marketplace RO — will frustrate you after the first year. Kent, Pureit (HUL), Eureka Forbes, and LG all have wide service networks in tier-1 and tier-2 cities. Aquaguard (Eureka Forbes) is wider in some South Indian cities; Kent is wider in the North and West; Pureit is comparable across metros. For tier-3 and rural buyers, the gap is bigger — Pureit and Aquaguard are usually the most reliable.

Our top 6 picks

⭐ Top Pick

1. Kent Grand Plus (11016)

Usually ₹14,500–₹17,500
Storage9 L tank
StagesRO+UV+UF
Recovery75%
NotesTDS controller, sediment filter

The Kent Grand Plus is the default RO water purifier in India for a reason. The 9 L tank suits a family of 4–5, the 75% recovery rate is the best in this price band, and the UV+UF post-treatment handles municipal supply well. Kent's service network is the widest in India with a 90-minute response time in most metros and a clean filter-tracking app.

Best for: anyone on municipal or borewell supply with TDS 300–2000 ppm who wants a credible brand-and-service combination. Verify the exact model code (11016) on the listing — Kent has more variants than any other brand and the older 11014 / 11015 are still being sold.

✓ What works

  • 75% recovery rate — best in class
  • 9 L tank suits a 4–5 person family
  • Kent's service network is the widest in India
  • UV+UF post-treatment handles municipal supply
  • TDS controller is included

✗ Trade-offs

  • Service AMC is ₹2,000–₹2,500/year
  • Filter changes need a technician visit (not DIY)
  • No mineral cartridge in the base kit

🥈 Best Value

2. Aquaguard Aura (100% RO+UV)

Usually ₹13,500–₹16,000
Storage7 L tank
StagesRO+UV+UF
Recovery60%
NotesTDS controller, mineral cartridge

The Aquaguard Aura is Eureka Forbes' mid-range RO+UV with a 7 L tank and slightly lower recovery rate than the Kent Grand Plus. The trade-off is a mineral cartridge included in the base kit, which adds calcium and magnesium back into the RO water and improves the taste noticeably. Aquaguard's service network is wider than Kent in some South Indian cities.

Best for: households that prefer Eureka Forbes' service network, or buyers who want a mineral cartridge in the base kit without paying for an upgrade. The 60% recovery rate is the main trade-off against the Kent Grand Plus.

✓ What works

  • Mineral cartridge included in the base kit
  • Aquaguard's service network is widest in South India
  • Active Copper Magneto technology filters copper-charged water
  • RO+UV+UF covers all input water types

✗ Trade-offs

  • 60% recovery rate — wastes more water than Kent Grand Plus
  • 7 L tank is tight for a 5-person family
  • AMC is ₹2,000–₹2,500/year
Check current price →
❄️ Tightest Budget

3. Pureit Copper+ Mineral RO (HUL)

Usually ₹12,500–₹15,000
Storage8 L tank
StagesRO+UV+MF
Recovery60%
NotesCopper cartridge, Germkill Kit

The Pureit Copper+ Mineral RO is HUL's premium RO purifier with an 8 L tank and a copper cartridge that infuses copper ions into the water. The Germkill Kit is a sealed filter assembly that is replaced as a whole — it can't be topped up with unauthorised filters, which is a real safety feature in markets where refilled filters are a known issue.

Best for: households that want a sealed-filter design (no chance of refilled / unauthorised filters) and a copper cartridge. Pureit's service network is the widest in tier-3 cities and rural India through Hindustan Unilever's distribution.

✓ What works

  • Sealed Germkill Kit — no refilled-filter risk
  • Pureit's service network is wide in tier-3 and rural India
  • Copper cartridge for taste
  • 8 L tank suits a 4–5 person family

✗ Trade-offs

  • 60% recovery rate
  • Germkill Kit replacement is more expensive than component filters
  • UV uses Micro Filtration (MF) instead of UF — slightly less effective
Check current price →

4. LG Puricare 8 L RO+UV Stainless Steel Tank

Usually ₹18,000–₹22,000
Storage8 L tank
StagesRO+UV+UF
Recovery75%
NotesDigital steriliser, stainless steel tank

The LG Puricare is the premium pick in this list. The 8 L stainless steel tank is more hygienic than the plastic tanks on Kent / Pureit / Aquaguard (less biofilm growth over time), and the digital steriliser runs an automatic UV cycle on the tank every 4 hours. The 75% recovery rate matches the Kent Grand Plus. LG's service network is strong in metros but less wide than Kent / Pureit outside tier-1 cities.

Best for: buyers who want a stainless steel tank and don't mind paying a premium for the digital steriliser. Worth it if you have an LG-warranty bundle or are willing to pay extra for the tank material.

✓ What works

  • Stainless steel tank — more hygienic
  • 75% recovery rate
  • Digital steriliser runs every 4 hours
  • True RO+UV+UF post-treatment

✗ Trade-offs

  • Premium price — ₹4,000–₹6,000 above the Kent Grand Plus
  • LG service network is narrower than Kent / Pureit outside metros
  • AMC is on the higher side at ₹2,500–₹3,500/year
Check current price →

5. Eureka Forbes Aquasure Aquaflo DX

Usually ₹9,500–₹12,000
Storage6 L tank
StagesRO+UV+MTDS
Recovery55%
NotesCompact wall-mount design

The Eureka Forbes Aquasure Aquaflo DX is the most affordable RO from a major brand in this list. The 6 L tank is tight for a larger family but works for a couple or a small nuclear family. The 55% recovery rate is on the lower side — wastes more water than the Kent Grand Plus or LG Puricare. The MTDS (Mineral TDS) controller is included.

Best for: buyers on a budget who want a credible branded RO around ₹10,000. Couples or small families on municipal supply with TDS under 800 ppm will get the best experience from this pick.

✓ What works

  • Most affordable RO from a major brand
  • Eureka Forbes' service network is reliable
  • MTDS controller included
  • Compact design suits small kitchens

✗ Trade-offs

  • 55% recovery rate — wastes more water
  • 6 L tank is tight for a 4+ person family
  • No UF stage — relies on UV for biological protection
Check current price →

The one we recommend skipping

⚠️ Skip

Sub-₹6,000 no-name RO purifiers from marketplace listings

Storage5–7 L tank
StagesRO only
RecoveryUnknown
NotesNo service network

Marketplace listings under ₹6,000 that promise RO+UV+UF with a 7 L tank and TDS controller are almost always built on Shenzhen reference designs. The membrane is smaller and lower-rejection than the membrane in a Kent or Pureit, the recovery rate is usually 30–40% (you waste 2 L of water for every 1 L purified), and the manufacturer disappears after the first 6 months — leaving you with no service network when the UV lamp dies or the membrane clogs.

We also recommend skipping any RO purifier that doesn't disclose the membrane brand (a real Dow / Vontron / CSM membrane is a positive signal) and that doesn't have a branded service network in your city. The cost of a single service visit from a local plumber after the warranty expires — usually ₹1,500–₹2,500 — often erases the price difference versus a major-brand RO that comes with annual AMC.

The bottom line

Buy the Kent Grand Plus (11016) if you want the most balanced RO water purifier in India for a family of 4–5: it leads on recovery rate, post-treatment, and service network reach. For a similar experience with a mineral cartridge in the base kit, the Aquaguard Aura is the closest alternative. The Pureit Copper+ Mineral RO is the right pick if you want a sealed-filter design and a wide service network in tier-3 cities.

For premium buyers who want a stainless steel tank and a digital steriliser, the LG Puricare 8 L is worth the ₹4,000–₹6,000 premium. The Eureka Forbes Aquasure Aquaflo DX is the budget pick around ₹10,000 for a couple or small family. Whatever you pick, sign up for the annual AMC in year 1 — it costs ₹2,000–₹3,500/year and covers all filter changes plus a free service visit.
